It solves the problem of efficiently preparing visibility data for temporal coherence by identifying blocks visible in the current frame and those newly visible since the last frame, enabling the selection of optimal occluders for subsequent rendering passes [S1, S2].

The claim states that the method solves the problem of efficiently preparing visibility data for temporal coherence by identifying blocks visible in the current frame and those newly visible since the last frame, enabling the selection of optimal occluders for subsequent rendering passes. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'we create both PVS_curr, which is used in the next frame to render the best occluders based on temporal coherence, and PVS_curr–prev, which determines the blocks which became visible since the last frame, in one common compute shader pass.' This directly supports every part of the claim: 1) 'efficiently preparing visibility data' is supported by the use of compute shaders for better utilization; 2) 'identifying blocks visible in the current frame' corresponds to PVS_curr; 3) 'those newly visible since the last frame' corresponds to PVS_curr-prev; 4) 'enabling the selection of optimal occluders for subsequent rendering passes' corresponds to 'used in the next frame to render the best occluders based on temporal coherence'. Source [S2] confirms these same facts.
